newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Teen-age Colombian brothers stage bogus kidnap.
newsitem.headline: Teen-age Colombian brothers stage bogus kidnap.

text.p: A pair of teenage brothers in Colombia's northern city of Bucaramanga staged a bogus kidnapping in a bid to win a $30,000 ransom from their mother, Bogota's El Espectador newspaper said on Friday.

It said one of the boys, aged 16, "disappeared" on May 27 after telling his mother he was going out to the movies. She later received repeated telephone calls demanding $30,000 in exchange for his release.

Police keeping tabs on the apparently suspicious movements of the 15-year-old brother who stayed home with his distraught mother followed him on repeated occasions to a house across town, the newspaper said.
It said anti-kidnapping police units raided the house earlier this week, only to find the "missing" brother comfortably hiding with a friend and playing dominoes.
The youth later confessed that he and his brother made up the abduction story in a bid to cash in on their mother's anguish.

Police could not be reached for immediate comment on the bizarre self-kidnapping case. But according to El Espectador the brothers were being held in a juvenile detention facility while the mother decided whether to press charges against them.
Colombia has what authorities describe as the world's highest kidnapping rate. The number of abductions increased 39 percent in 1996 over the previous year to a total of 1,608, police said.
